target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget.

The shared chat UI pending/completion wait uses the same five-minute window, and macOS WebChat now waits for completion through existing Gateway `agent.wait` before refreshing history. The change uses existing Gateway surfaces (`chat.send.timeoutMs` and `agent.wait`) and does not change gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window.

## Evidence

Native macOS visual/accessibility proof on the PR build, using the native `OpenClaw Chat` window and a session-level `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` override for this proof run:

```text
submitted_at_local=2026-07-05 14:48:31 CST
prompt=For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly `sleep 45` with no output, then reply exactly `native WebChat slow reply proof complete`.
```

At +32 seconds, the native macOS window was still connected and still showed the assistant pending state instead of a 30-second timeout/error:

```text
pending_capture_at_local=2026-07-05 14:49:03 CST
AXWindow name='OpenClaw Chat' desc='standard window'
  AXGroup
    AXScrollArea
      AXOpaqueProviderGroup desc='list'
        AXStaticText value='For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly sleep 45 with no output, then reply exactly native WebChat slow reply proof complete.'
        AXStaticText value='Agent avatar'
        AXStaticText value='Writing'
    AXStaticText value='Gateway connected'
```

After the slow run completed, the same native window cleared the pending state and showed the final assistant reply:

```text
completion_capture_at_local=2026-07-05 14:49:38 CST
AXWindow name='OpenClaw Chat' desc='standard window'
  AXGroup
    AXScrollArea
      AXOpaqueProviderGroup desc='list'
        AXStaticText value='For local PR #97722 native WebChat visual proof only: use the shell tool to run exactly sleep 45 with no output, then reply exactly native WebChat slow reply proof complete.'
        AXStaticText value='Agent avatar'
        AXStaticText value='native WebChat slow reply proof complete'
    AXStaticText value='Gateway connected'
```

Latest conflict-resolution validation after rebasing onto current `origin/main`:

```text
changed_files= 5
conflict_markers=none
PASS: webchat explicit timeout
PASS: agent wait uses injected gateway
PASS: compact uses injected gateway
PASS: compact disables retry
PASS: compact validates response
PASS: GatewayConnection.chatSend default is request-sized
PASS: sendMessageStatus defaults started and terminal ok explicit
```

```text
diff_check=clean
merge_tree=clean
merge_tree_output=[local path redacted]
```

Timeout-scope regression proof from the final scope fix:

```text
PASS: GatewayConnection.chatSend default is request-sized
PASS: MacGatewayChatTransport explicitly opts into 300000ms
PASS: low-level default regression expects 30000
PASS: mac transport regression expects 300000
```

The timeout-scope check was first run as a RED proof before the production fix and failed with:

```text
RED: timeout scope invariant not satisfied
- GatewayConnection.chatSend default is not request-sized
- MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage does not explicitly opt into 300000ms
```

Regression coverage added or updated:

- `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayConnectionControlTests.swift` asserts the low-level `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default remains `timeoutMs == 30000`, `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` sends `timeoutMs == 300_000`, macOS WebChat delegates completion waits to Gateway `agent.wait`, and `agent.wait` receives the supplied run ID and timeout.
- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift` asserts shared chat completion waits use `300_000` ms, keeps non-terminal send ACKs pending by default, and keeps the terminal `ok` ACK case explicit.

Local Swift execution is unavailable in this Linux environment:

```text
swift unavailable: command not found
swiftformat unavailable: command not found
xcodebuild unavailable: command not found
```

Hosted macOS CI should execute the Swift tests and formatter on the updated PR head.
